newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close above lows after Wall St gain.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close above lows after Wall St gain.

text.p: Dutch shares closed above the day's lows on Thursday after a volatile session which saw prices dip after a batch of U.S. economic data, only to come back up slightly in the wake of a Wall Street rise.
The AEX share index closed 1.84 points lower at 795.02, dragged below Wednesday's record high closing at the outset by weaker bonds and an ex-dividend decline in Royal Dutch.

Shares dipped to the session low of 790.11 just after the U.S. figures, which showed a smaller than anticipated increase in jobless claims. A 0.1 percent rise in April consumer prices came within expectations and had little direct impact.

"The CPI was OK, it came within expectations and isn't showing many signs of inflation," a dealer said. "But the market didn't like the jobs figures because they showed signs of a stronger economy than people had reckoned on," he added.
He added, however, that the figures would probably not be enough to prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten interest rates at next Tuesday's Open Market Committee meeting.

"We don't think the Fed will increase rates next week because the economic growth we've seen in recent figures is relatively benign," he said, adding that unchanged U.S. rates were reflected in current Dutch share prices.

Dealers said a push up towards the 800 level on the AEX could come on Friday if Wall Street rose convincingly overnight, although stiff resistance could come out of the options market ahead of Friday's derivatives expirations.
"We're hearing from the options market that a lot of people will lose money if the index is settled above 800 at the expiration," said a dealer.

Others said the market had strong underlying fundamentals and it was only a matter of time before the 800 level fell. "There's no big reason we shouldn't go through 800 or further," another dealer said.
